item.title: Rail operator pledges improvements to Fen Line services
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Rail operator pledges improvements to Fen Line services
Great Northern has acknowledged that recent performance on the King’s Lynn Fen Line has been challenging for passengers. The operator says it is working to rebuild customer confidence following a rise in cancellations during September. North West Norfolk MP James Wild has been meeting with rail executives to press for better reliability, citing the impact of disruptions on commuters.
The operator reports that cancellations on the route fell by two-thirds between late September and mid-October. Efforts are now underway to improve fleet reliability and staff availability. The company is also working to restore a normal timetable between Ely and King’s Lynn once speed restrictions caused by ground conditions are lifted.

item.title: Hundreds protest against potential service cuts at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Hundreds protest against potential service cuts at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
Hundreds of people gathered in King’s Lynn’s Tuesday Market Place last Saturday to protest against leaked proposals to downgrade A&E, maternity, and intensive care services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital. North West Norfolk MP James Wild attended the demonstration, describing it as a powerful show of community support.
Mr Wild has raised concerns in the House of Commons regarding the hospital's performance and the lack of transparency surrounding the potential service changes. He argued that removing local access to care would disadvantage residents in rural and coastal areas. The MP has called on the Health Secretary to reject any plans to reduce services, insisting that NHS bosses must prioritise the needs of local patients and maintain accessible care.

item.title: King’s Lynn man fined for driving without a licence
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn man fined for driving without a licence
A 22-year-old man from North Lynn has been banned from driving for six months after being caught behind the wheel without a licence or insurance. Gentjan Capani, of Loke Road, was stopped by police on Tennyson Road on September 30. Officers had initially pulled the vehicle over due to suspicions regarding drugs, though no further details on that matter were provided.
Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Capani admitted to the offences. He told the court he is an asylum seeker without the right to work in the UK. In addition to the driving ban, he was ordered to pay a £120 fine, a £48 victim surcharge, and £50 in court costs.

Former Wisbech Town FC president returns to watch match
A resident of Orchard House Care Home in Wisbech has enjoyed a special return to his former football club. John Petch, who served as president of Wisbech Town Football Club for 16 years before stepping down in 2020, expressed a wish to see his hometown team play once more. Staff from the care home arranged for Mr Petch and his wife, Sheila, to attend Saturday’s match, which included lunch at Bygones. Mr Petch, who spent nearly 60 years at the club, was greeted by many familiar faces, including chairman Paul Brenchley. He described the experience as a fantastic day and expressed his pride in seeing the team secure a victory.

item.title: King’s Lynn man admits to car park arson
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn man admits to car park arson
A 21-year-old man from King’s Lynn has pleaded guilty to arson following a fire at the St James Multistory Car Park. Dylan Jenkins-Drewery, of Gaywood Road, admitted to setting fire to toilet rolls while inside a cubicle on September 6. Norfolk Fire and Rescue Service attended the scene within 30 minutes to extinguish the flames, which caused damage to the cubicle and a toilet roll holder.
CCTV footage captured the defendant leaving the area shortly before smoke was spotted. At Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, the court heard that Jenkins-Drewery had been playing with a lighter. The case has been adjourned for a pre-sentence report, and he is due to be sentenced on December 15.

item.title: West Norfolk and Breckland schools feature in unofficial league table
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
West Norfolk and Breckland schools feature in unofficial league table
A new unofficial league table published by The Telegraph has rated several schools across West Norfolk and Breckland as below average. The rankings, based on a 40-point system using 2025/26 academic data, placed Springwood High School in King’s Lynn as the area’s top performer with a rating of good. Downham Market Academy and Fakenham Academy were both rated as fair.
However, local education trusts have questioned the findings. Representatives argued that the rankings fail to capture the full context of school improvement or the progress made by pupils. Marshland High School’s head teacher, Craig Jansen, criticised the methodology, suggesting it does not fairly account for the socioeconomic challenges faced by schools serving disadvantaged communities.

item.title: Concerns grow over potential maternity service cuts in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Concerns grow over potential maternity service cuts in King’s Lynn
Campaigners and MPs have raised alarms over the future of maternity services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. The facility is being reviewed by the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group, which is considering centralising services at the Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital.
The Queen Elizabeth and the James Paget Hospital in Gorleston are among the 12 smallest consultant-led maternity units in England. While hospital bosses state no decisions have been made, critics warn that potential closures would force women to travel longer distances for care. A clinical strategy regarding the future of these services is expected to be presented to the Norfolk County Council’s health overview and scrutiny committee next month.

📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Plans submitted for 80-bed care home in King’s Lynn
A planning application has been submitted to West Norfolk Council for a new 80-bed care home in King’s Lynn. Proposed by Kori Developments Ltd, the facility would be located off the Queen Elizabeth Way roundabout, adjacent to Mintlyn Crematorium. The site would feature en-suite bedrooms, communal areas including a café and hair salon, and 32 parking spaces.
Developers state the project aims to address a local shortage of elderly care provision and is expected to create 80 jobs, with up to 25 staff on-site at any time. If approved, the home will provide dementia, respite, and end-of-life care. A decision on the proposal is expected by January 22.
